items.abstract: <jats:p>Benign-trained anomaly detection is attractive for UAV security because it avoids dependence on predefined attack signatures, but deployment also requires a threshold that preserves the intended false alarm rate (FAR). This study separates score discrimination from threshold reliability and evaluates how benign calibration data are selected and refreshed. On the UAV Attack Dataset, a transferred detector retained useful discrimination while its source-platform threshold produced a 96.0% FAR.Recalibration using benign target observations reduced FAR to 5.0% without refitting the scoring model. We then evaluated eight anomaly detectors on public PX4 flight logs comprising 325 airframes and 1,815 flights in exploratory and preregistered confirmatory panels. Thresholds calibrated from the initial segment of a flight were less reliable than thresholds based on observations distributed across the flight or refreshed during operation. In the confirmatory panel, 4.085% of leading-segment calibration cases exceeded a 50% FAR, whereas no such failures occurred under dispersed calibration.At a matched calibration budget, no alternative calibration operator reduced matched-FAR attack detection by more than 0.002 relative to leading calibration. Cross-airframe transfer increased tail risk over cross-session transfer in the nine-topic representation but not in the GNSS-only representation. Although evaluated on UAV telemetry, the study highlights a broader deployment issue for benign- trained monitoring in IoT and cyber-physical systems: decision thresholds may not remain reliable across devices, sessions, and changing operating conditions.</jats:p>
title: Calibration Design for Reliable False-Alarm Control in Benign-Trained UAV Anomaly Detection

items.abstract: This thesis addresses deep learning-based methods for automatic anomaly detection in an industrial context. It involves image- or sensor-based detection of defects in the production process that can affect the quality of products. Automating this task provides a reliable and cost-effective alternative to humans, who perform this task manually by sighting. Since this setup has special requirements such as detecting previously unknown defects that traditional approaches cannot fulfill, this paper presents anomaly detection methods that learn without any examples of anomalies and include only normal data in the training process. Most of our proposed methods address the problem from a statistical perspective. Based on a deep-learning-based density estimation of the normal data, it is assumed that anomalies are considered unlikely according to the modeled distribution. The density estimation is performed by socalled Normalizing Flows, which, in contrast to conventional neural networks, can model a formally valid probability distribution due to their bijective mapping. title: Industrial Anomaly Detection with Normalizing Flows

items.abstract: <jats:p>We propose a unsupservised approach to anomaly detection in data with a temporal dimension. We adapt the VAE-GAN architecture to learn the proxy task of temporal sequence continuation. Rather than reconstructing the input, our variational decoder decodes to a forecast of the future sequence. In order to separate structural uncertainty (which our model can reconstruct by fitting to observed data) from stochastic uncertainty (which it cannot) we introduce an additional decoder that outputs the pointwise confidence of the prediction, after the optimal latent-variable has been found. We can use this for zero-shot anomaly detection, separating anomalies from stochastic variation that cannot be modelled, without any examples. We introduce a new dataset comprising linescan imagery of railway lines which we use to illustrate our methods and achieve state-of-the-art on the ECG5000 time series anomaly detection dataset.</jats:p>
title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection with a Temporal Continuation, Confidence-Aware Vae-Gan

items.abstract: <jats:p>Anomaly detection is essential for ensuring the operational safety and mission availability of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). Existing methods usually construct anomaly detection models by learning normal flight patterns from training data. However, they commonly assume that the training set is purely normal and often lack explicit anomaly priors. In practical UAV systems, training data are frequently contaminated by unlabeled anomalies or strong noise, which can distort normality modeling and lead to a biased decision boundary. To address this problem, this paper proposes a dual calibration network, termed DualCal, for confident UAV anomaly detection. DualCal constructs a compact normal state hypersphere in the feature space and calibrates its boundary through two complementary modules. The uncertainty guided penalty module adaptively reduces the optimization weight of low confidence samples to suppress the influence of contaminated data, while the synthetic anomaly perturbation module generates diverse synthetic anomalies to provide anomaly aware supervision and sharpen the decision boundary. Experiments on two UAV datasets demonstrate that DualCal consistently outperforms 12 state-of-the-art baselines under both clean and contaminated training conditions, confirming its superior detection accuracy and robustness.</jats:p>
title: Confident Detection: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Anomaly Detection under Data Contamination via Uncertainty Calibration

items.abstract: <jats:p>Point cloud downsampling in RGB-D industrial anomaly localization is commonly treated as a task-agnostic input compression step. However, farthest point sampling (FPS) primarily optimizes global geometric coverage, which is not necessarily aligned with the objective of retaining sparse defect evidence under a fixed sampling budget. To address this mismatch, we propose Prior-Aware Sampling (PAS), which jointly considers point selection and anomaly score calibration. PAS first derives an intra-image feature deviation prior from a frozen DINOv2 model and transfers the prior to the aligned 3D point set through pixel-to-point correspondences. A hybrid sampling strategy then allocates the fixed budget among prior-guided sampling, random exploration, and global FPS, while FPS within the prior-selected candidate pool preserves the spatial diversity of high-response centers. To account for the resulting non-uniform center distribution, PAS further converts local center coverage into a density response and uses it to calibrate point-wise 3D anomaly scores. Across five 3D backbones on MVTec 3D-AD, PAS improves the mean point-level AUROC (PtAUC) from 0.7693 to 0.8065 and the mean area under the per-region-overlap curve (AUPRO) from 0.4672 to 0.5187. For PointNet++, the defect-point coverage at the first sampling bottleneck increases from 1.46% to 16.08%. Prior-disruption and component-ablation experiments further confirm the importance of valid 2D-3D correspondence and the complementary effects of hybrid sampling and coverage-aware calibration. Experiments on Eyecandies and Real-IAD D³ also show positive average gains under external data distributions and real industrial acquisition conditions.</jats:p>
title: Cross-modal prior-guided sampling with coverage-aware score calibration for 3D industrial anomaly localization

items.abstract: <jats:p>Encrypted QUIC anomaly detection faces two deployment problems that fixed detectors handle poorly: cross-environment cold-start, where no session-specific calibration is yet available, and calibration instability, where threshold reliability depends on destination-server diversity rather than raw warm-up volume. We present an adaptive, calibration-aware NIDS that switches among three detector modes using a single observable variable, the count of distinct destination-window groups accumulated during benign warm-up. The core model is a two-view masked edge-reconstruction graph neural network pre-trained on benign CESNET QUIC traffic and adapted to the Kadi dataset using only benign data; no attack labels are used at any training stage. In Mode 1, only the source-view graph component is active and transfers across environments with approximately 5 % false-positive rate. In Mode 2, the full two-view graph detector uses session-specific calibration; a shrinkage refinement was evaluated but showed no consistent benefit and is reported as a negative result. In Mode 3 (ndst≥ 30), an OR-hybrid combining the graph detector with a Kitsune-style AfterImage autoencoder achieves the best warm-start performance. On Session D at 20 % warm-up (ndst = 105), the OR-hybrid reaches 99.9 % SCAN recall at 4.6 % FPR, outperforming the graph detector alone (97.8 % at 6.6 % FPR) and Kitsune alone (47.6 % at 4.2 % FPR). On Session C at 30 % warm-up (ndst = 18), a Mode 2 ablation with the OR-hybrid reaches 94.1 % SCAN recall at 3.3 % FPR, showing that graph destination-view structure remains valuable even below the Mode 3 stability threshold.</jats:p>
title: Adaptive Calibration-Aware Anomaly Detection for Encrypted QUIC Traffic

items.abstract: <jats:p>Anomaly detection is essential for ensuring the operational safety and mission availability of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). Existing methods usually construct anomaly detection models by learning normal flight patterns from training data. However, they commonly assume that the training set is purely normal and often lack explicit anomaly priors. In practical UAV systems, training data are frequently contaminated by unlabeled anomalies or strong noise, which can distort normality modeling and lead to a biased decision boundary. To address this problem, this paper proposes a dual calibration network, termed DualCal, for confident UAV anomaly detection. DualCal constructs a compact normal state hypersphere in the feature space and calibrates its boundary through two complementary modules. The uncertainty guided penalty module adaptively reduces the optimization weight of low confidence samples to suppress the influence of contaminated data, while the synthetic anomaly perturbation module generates diverse synthetic anomalies to provide anomaly aware supervision and sharpen the decision boundary. Experiments on two UAV datasets demonstrate that DualCal consistently outperforms 12 state-of-the-art baselines under both clean and contaminated training conditions, confirming its superior detection accuracy and robustness.</jats:p>
title: Confident Detection: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Anomaly Detection under Data Contamination via Uncertainty Calibration

items.abstract: <jats:p>Weakly-supervised video anomaly detection (WS-VAD) only requires video-level labels for training, making it suitable for large-scale surveillance scenarios. However, existing methods suffer from gradient conflicts in multi-branch feature fusion, insufficient exploitation of predictive uncertainty, and an imbalance between long-range temporal modeling and computational efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes the DUC-Former model. In this model, a global-local hybrid spatio-temporal Transformer encoder is designed to capture long-range dependencies with linear complexity; a gradient-matching stabilized differentiable architecture search strategy (DARTS-GM) is proposed to automatically optimize the fusion of features and uncertainty; an uncertainty-weighted multiple instance learning framework is constructed to focus on hard examples; and a temporal-semantic dual-aware contrastive learning strategy is developed to jointly model temporal distance and feature similarity. Theoretically, we prove the Bayesian optimality condition for feature magnitude learning and derive the generalization bound of the dynamic feature bank. Experiments demonstrate that DUC-Former achieves 88.3% ± 0.5% frame-level AUC on the UCF-Crime dataset and realizes 55 FPS real-time inference with 17W power consumption on the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge device, accompanied by an expected calibration error (ECE) of only 3.2%. The results validate the superiority of the proposed method in both performance and efficiency.</jats:p>
title: DUC-Former: Dynamic Uncertainty Calibration with Neural Architecture Search for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection

items.abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) in industrial inspection aims to identifyabnormal patterns using only normal training samples. Existing pseudo-anomalysynthesis methods either construct visible defects in image space or perturb asingle feature distribution, which limits their ability to model theheterogeneous geometry of structural defects and semantic deviations. This paperproposes a boundary-aware structural--semantic pseudo anomaly learning frameworkin feature space. The proposed method decomposes pretrained embeddings intomid-level structural and high-level semantic subspaces and applies layer-matchedperturbation operators to synthesize complementary pseudo anomalies. RefinedGaussian perturbation is used to model local structural irregularities, whilecenter-outward extrapolation is applied to high-level semantic features toemulate distributional shifts. A dual-head discriminator is further introducedto jointly learn anomaly confidence and pseudo-boundary consistency, whereboundary labels are derived from the known synthetic mask rather than predictionthresholds. During inference, the training-only synthesis and refinementoperations are removed, yielding a lightweight feature-discriminator scoringpipeline. Experiments on standard industrial anomaly detection benchmarksdemonstrate competitive image-level detection and improved pixel-levellocalization, validating the effectiveness of the proposed feature-spacepseudo-anomaly learning strategy.
title: Boundary-Aware Structural-Semantic Pseudo Anomaly Learning for Industrial Anomaly Detection

items.abstract: <jats:p>In the field of Machine Learning (ML), transitioning from univariate monitoring to a multivariate framework allows for a sophisticated analysis of complex industrial systems. While a bivariate model simultaneously evaluates two related sensors, such as temperature and humidity, the trivariate normal distribution enables the inclusion of a third critical variable, such as air pressure, to establish a more robust dynamic mathematical baseline for operational normality. This research presents a paradigm shift in industrial monitoring by transitioning from rigid, static threshold systems to a framework of probabilistic intelligence. By deriving the trivariate scaling factor and inverse covariance matrix, the model can distinguish between benign stochastic fluctuations and genuine early-stage hardware malfunctions with high granularity. The study demonstrates that by understanding how three sensors dance together through covariance, systems can identify contextual anomalies that individually appear normal but statistically violate the learned operational relationship.</jats:p>
title: Trivariate Normal Distribution in Machine Learning for Industrial Anomaly Detection

items.abstract: <jats:p>Weakly supervised video anomaly detection (WSVAD) has attracted increasing attention due to its low annotation cost and practical applicability in large-scale video analysis. Although existing methods have achieved promising performance, they still suffer from difficult discriminability of hard samples due to severe feature coupling in feature space. To address this issues, we propose a weakly supervised video anomaly detection framework based on feature disentanglement and confidence-aware scoring. Specifically, we enhance the separability of difficult samples by disentangling representations into normal and abnormal features, enabling subtle anomaly cues hidden in entangled regions to be more effectively perceived. Furthermore, a Confidence-Aware MIL strategy is designed to dynamically sharpen scores of hard anomalies with disentangled abnormal features, thereby strengthening the model’s ability to distinguish ambiguous samples. Through the joint of feature disentanglement and confidence-aware scoring, the proposed framework progressively improves anomaly representation learning and hard sample discrimination under weak supervision. Extensive experiments on the XD-Violence and UCF-Crime datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance.</jats:p>
title: Feature Disentanglement and Confidence-Aware MIL for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection

items.abstract: <jats:p>Few-shot industrial anomaly detection requires a reliable alarm threshold when only defect-free samples are available. Frozen visual features improve data efficiency, but a high AUROC does not itself define a deployable operating point. We propose CAL-FrozenAD, a training-free framework that fuses nearest-neighbor patch distances from texture-sensitive and semantic layers and calibrates the image score by split conformal prediction. Under exchangeable normal data, the resulting threshold controls the marginal false-alarm probability at a user-selected level; the same fused map provides pixel localization. In one-shot experiments on MVTec AD, VisA, and Real-IAD, CAL-FrozenAD reaches 80.5% mean image AUROC and 80.5% mean recall at a nominal 5% false-alarm level, improving the strongest baseline by 0.5 and 2.6 percentage points, respectively, with 1.4 ms/image additional inference time.</jats:p>
title: Calibrated few-shot industrial anomaly detection with frozen visual features

items.abstract: <jats:p>This research presents a paradigm shift in industrial monitoring by transitioning from rigid, static threshold systems to a framework of probabilistic intelligence. Modern industrial processes are characterized by inherent stochasticity and natural fluctuations that traditional hard-coded constraints often misidentify as failures, leading to high false alarm rates. By integrating the Univariate Gaussian Probability Density Function (PDF) directly into machine learning architectures, a dynamic mathematical baseline for operational normality is established. The study employs Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) to analyze historical data. This allows the model to learn the unique environmental noise of a system, such as temperature variations in a server room, and calculate a continuous score of suspicion.</jats:p>
title: Machine Learning for Industrial Anomaly Detection: A Probabilistic Intelligence Approach
